terms.d: Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation. A proxy for operating cash generation, and the main yardstick for infrastructure because depreciation is large.
How many years of operating cash it would take to repay net debt. APSEZ caps itself at 2.5x; renewable developers in build mode run 5–6x.
Enterprise value divided by EBITDA. The standard multiple for infrastructure M&A; APSEZ paid 11.7x CY25 for Evos.
Annualised EBITDA of the assets already operating, including those commissioned only recently. AGEL uses it for leverage ratios.
PAT plus depreciation, deferred tax and exceptional items. AGEL reports it to show cash generation that accounting profit hides.
Capital expenditure relative to revenue or EBITDA. It explains why financing access is the central constraint for the group.
A contract in which the customer pays for reserved capacity whether it uses it or not. It underpins Evos and many port and gas contracts.
Power Purchase Agreement. A long-term (often 25-year) contract to sell power at a fixed or formula tariff to a discom or corporate buyer.
Power Supply Agreement. The thermal-side equivalent of a PPA (for example, Adani Power's 1,320 MW PSA with Uttarakhand).
Letter of Award. The buyer's notice that a bid has won; the formal PPA or contract follows.
Tariff-Based Competitive Bidding. Transmission and storage projects are awarded to the lowest annual tariff bid for 35 years; this is how AESL wins its lines.
Renewable round-the-clock power. Renewables combined with storage or other sources to supply firm power around the clock (for example, AESL's WBSEDCL award).
Firm and Dispatchable Renewable Energy. Tenders requiring renewables to meet demand-following supply profiles.
Plant Load Factor. Actual output as a share of the maximum possible for thermal plants; Adani Power ran at 70.1% in Q2 FY27.
Capacity Utilisation Factor. The renewable equivalent of PLF; solar typically runs 20–30%, wind 25–40%.
When the grid cannot absorb generation and the plant is told to back down. Lost revenue for renewables, and a symptom of weak transmission.
Battery Energy Storage System, measured in MW (power) and MWh/GWh (energy). AGEL had 6.63 GWh installed by Q2 FY27.
Pumped Storage Project. Water is pumped uphill when power is cheap and released through turbines when it is needed. Tarali is AGEL's 1,500 MW PSP.
Inter-State Transmission System. Its charge waiver for renewables tapers 25% a year after June 2025.
Circuit kilometres. Transmission line length multiplied by the number of circuits; AESL operates about 29,800 ckm.
Distribution company that sells power to end consumers (for example AEML in Mumbai). Discom finances drive payment risk for generators.
Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (2021). Central scheme funding loss reduction and about 20 crore smart meters.
Aggregate Technical and Commercial losses: power that is lost or not billed or collected. Smart meters aim to reduce them.
Coal linkage allocation policy that gives power plants assured coal supply tied to PPAs.
Nuclear law notified in December 2025 that opens nuclear power to licensed private players. Its rules are still being framed.
Production Linked Incentive. Subsidies tied to domestic manufacturing output (solar modules, battery cells); relevant to ANIL.
Million metric tonnes (cargo handled) / million tonnes per annum (capacity: ports, cement).
Twenty-foot equivalent unit, the standard measure of container volume.
Water depth at a berth. Deeper draft lets larger ships call; Mundra and Vizhinjam are deep-draft ports.
Moving cargo from one ship to another at a hub port. Vizhinjam aims to capture India's transshipment that today goes via Colombo and Singapore.
Multi-Modal Logistics Park, linking rail, road and warehousing inland; part of APSEZ's 'shore-to-door' offering.
Special Economic Zone, an industrial land area with tax and customs benefits. Mundra SEZ hosts group manufacturing.
Aero comes from regulated landing and passenger charges (set by AERA). Non-aero comes from retail, F&B, parking and city-side real estate, which drives airport value.
Airports Economic Regulatory Authority. It sets aeronautical tariffs at major airports.
In aviation, Air Traffic Movement: one take-off or landing.
Very large data-centre capacity leased to cloud and AI firms; measured in MW of IT load, not square feet.
Power Usage Effectiveness: total facility power divided by IT power. Lower is better, with 1.2–1.4 considered efficient.
The key cement metric. Ambuja targets about ₹4,000 per tonne by FY28 through green power, logistics and fuel savings.
The intermediate product of a cement kiln, ground with gypsum or fly ash to make cement. Clinker capacity limits cement capacity.
A plant that grinds clinker into cement close to markets, cutting lead distance and freight costs.
Waste Heat Recovery System, which generates power from kiln exhaust heat. It is part of cement decarbonisation.
SEBI Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements regulations, which govern related-party disclosures and other listed-company obligations.
Minimum Public Shareholding: listed companies must keep at least 25% public float. It was the subject of a SEBI order in September 2026.
A proceeding disposed of on payment without admitting or denying wrongdoing. SEBI can restore it if representations prove untrue.
A US case dismissal that bars refiling the same claims. It is not a factual finding of innocence.
National Board for Wildlife. It must clear projects in or near protected areas or eco-sensitive zones (the issue at Tarali).
National Company Law Tribunal. It sanctions mergers such as Ambuja with ACC and Orient.
Adani's practice of starting new businesses inside AEL and separating them (listing or demerger) once mature.
Selling minority stakes in operating assets to long-term investors to fund new builds, as in Adani Airports with 360 ONE.

facts.q: What is APSEZ's ceiling for net debt to EBITDA?
facts.a: Up to 2.5x. It was 1.8x at Q2 FY27, and about 2.76x pro forma with Evos.

facts.q: AGEL's operational renewable capacity at H1 FY27?
facts.a: 20.8 GW, with 6.63 GWh of BESS. The target is 50 GW by 2030.

facts.q: What did APSEZ agree to buy in November 2026, and at what value?
facts.a: Evos B.V., a European liquid-storage operator with 8 terminals in 5 countries, at an enterprise value of €2.56 bn (11.7x EV/EBITDA).

facts.q: Domestic ports EBITDA margin in Q2 FY27?
APSEZ's all-India cargo and container share (Q2 FY27)?
Adani Power's operating capacity and Q2 FY27 PLF?
facts.a: 18,150 MW at a 70.1% PLF, with 23,720 MW under expansion.

facts.q: AESL's transmission orderbook?
facts.a: ₹87,222 cr under construction across 15 projects, plus 24.6 mn smart meters on order.

facts.q: Ambuja's cement capacity now, and its targets?
facts.a: 113.5 MTPA now, 119 MTPA by March 2027 and 155 MTPA by FY30 (₹14,500 cr of capex).

facts.q: What happened on 22 September 2026 at SEBI?
facts.a: A settlement order disposed of the related-party disclosure (LODR) adjudication against five Adani companies, on payment of about ₹1.5 cr.

facts.q: What did the US court do on 10 August 2026?
facts.a: It dismissed the criminal case with prejudice after DOJ moved to drop it. This bars refiling but is not a finding of innocence.

facts.q: What is the OFAC settlement?
facts.a: AEL agreed to a $275m settlement (May 2026) for apparent Iran-sanctions violations, booked as ₹2,644 cr one-time in Q1 FY27.

facts.q: Why was work stopped at Tarali?
facts.a: Maharashtra's forest department said work began without NBWL wildlife approval. It also emerged that the cost submitted to the department had been cut from ₹5,675 cr to ₹56.75 cr. AGEL contests both points.

facts.q: Who is the Group CFO?
Who is CEO of APSEZ?
facts.a: Ashwani Gupta (Whole-Time Director and CEO). Karan Adani is MD.

facts.q: Who heads AGEL and ANIL?
facts.a: Vneet S. Jaain: MD of AGEL and CEO of ANIL.

facts.q: When did Navi Mumbai International Airport start operations?
facts.a: Commercial operations began on 25 December 2025; international flights followed in July 2026.

facts.q: What valuation did 360 ONE's investment imply for Adani Airports?
facts.a: About $18 bn, for roughly 1.55% at ₹2,790 cr (media reports).

facts.q: AdaniConneX: operational and tied-up capacity?
facts.a: 94.6 MW operational and 1.2+ GW tied up, including a 240 MW Navi Mumbai hyperscale order.

facts.q: What is the ISTS waiver status for new solar and wind?
facts.a: Full waiver ended for projects commissioned after 30 June 2025; it now tapers 25% a year to zero after June 2028.

facts.q: What is the group's one-line strategic thesis?
facts.a: Originate, build, operate and integrate infrastructure across adjacent value chains, with AEL as incubator, and now extend physical infrastructure into digital and AI infrastructure.
